description: Hype&Hyper is a Budapest annual about Central and Eastern Europe, covering strategy, business, design and lifestyle from the region's own point of view. Each themed print issue mixes essays on geopolitics and regional economies with design, architecture, food and art features, in English and Hungarian. It is for readers interested in the culture and business of the region.

Inque is a large format annual literary and arts magazine printed without advertising and planned as a ten issue run. Each number is divided into non fiction, fiction, interviews and art and runs to around 220 pages of new writing from established novelists and essayists alongside commissioned artwork. It is for readers who collect literary print and want long reads in a heavyweight object.

It's Freezing in LA! is a British magazine about the climate crisis that pairs essays and reportage with commissioned illustration, each issue built around a theme such as plants, knowledge or power. Issues run to about sixty pages and bring together writing on energy, politics, ecology and culture by emerging writers. It is for readers who want longer, idea led climate writing with a strong visual identity.

Italy Segreta is a large format annual grown out of an English language website about Italian travel, food and everyday culture. Each volume takes a single theme, most recently the generations, and fills about 124 pages with photo essays by Italian photographers alongside reported stories and interviews, in two cover variants. It suits readers who follow Italy through regional food, design and street life rather than guidebooks.

Jewish Currents is an American quarterly of left wing Jewish politics, culture and ideas, founded in 1946, carrying long reported pieces on Israel and Palestine, American politics and the far right alongside essays, fiction, poetry, comics and art criticism. Print issues reach subscribers first and go online later. It suits readers interested in diaspora politics and left movements who want magazine length writing.

Kink is a small format, bilingual Spanish and English photography magazine devoted to the male nude, shot in natural light in domestic interiors and landscapes. Each issue comes packaged with a short text supplement, the Cuaderno, and usually appears with more than one cover. It suits collectors of gay erotic and independent photography publishing.

Le Matricule des Anges is a French language monthly devoted to contemporary literature, built around a themed dossier on a writer or movement plus review sections for fiction, poetry, essays, theatre and illustrated books. It runs ten issues a year and gives subscribers an online archive back to 1992. It suits French readers who follow small press and translated literature closely.

leafie is a British print magazine about cannabis, psychedelics and the culture around them, spun out of a daily news site on the same subjects. Each issue is a PUR bound volume of around 120 pages mixing long reads on drug history and policy with interviews with growers, artists and researchers, with a European rather than North American focus. It suits readers interested in drug reform and psychedelic research who want it in print.

Literary Review of Canada is a journal of ideas built around long book reviews and essays on politics, history, science, literature and culture, with commissioned cover art and poetry in each number. It appears ten times a year in a review format and keeps a full online archive for print subscribers. It suits readers who want sustained, review led coverage of Canadian writing and public debate.

Little White Lies builds each print issue around one new film, with a commissioned illustrated cover and a long run of interviews and essays on that release before turning to reviews and features on the rest of cinema. The illustration heavy design has been its signature since 2005. It is for readers who follow arthouse and mainstream cinema and want criticism with a strong visual identity.

Log is a text led journal of architectural criticism and commentary from New York that covers buildings, cities, technology and design culture through essays, interviews and short observations rather than image spreads. Issues are mostly open themed with occasional thematic numbers, three times a year. It is for architects, students and scholars who follow architectural thinking closely.

LOST is a bilingual English and Chinese travel annual built around first person stories of self discovery rather than destination guides, with around ten long personal narratives per issue and commissioned photography. It is printed as a thick volume on uncoated paper. It suits readers who like slow, reflective travel writing and Chinese language perspectives on travel.

LoveWant is a large format Sydney fashion, photography and art magazine with multiple collectable covers per issue, built from portraits, fashion stories shot by its own editors and interviews with musicians and artists. Text is sparse and the 240 pages read as a printed moodboard. It is for fashion image collectors and people who follow photographers and models rather than trends.

Maisonneuve is a Montreal general interest quarterly that mixes reported features on social and political questions with essays, fiction, poetry and comics, plus review sections on books, music and film and some work translated from Quebec French. Each issue carries a cover story on a current Canadian subject. It suits readers who want long form Canadian journalism and literary writing in one magazine.

MilK is a French language quarterly about family life with children, covering children's fashion, interiors and home tours, design objects, travel and parenting. Photographic fashion stories sit alongside features on makers and artists, and covers usually show a family or child in a styled home. It is for style conscious parents.

More or Less is a large format fashion magazine built around the idea of consuming less, mixing vintage, surplus, sportswear, uniform and craft clothing with current season pieces in long photographic stories. Issues are themed, run to several hundred pages and appear with multiple covers. It is for fashion readers and image makers interested in sustainability and styling rather than shopping.

Musicworks is a Toronto magazine about experimental music and sound art, with long profiles of composers, improvisers and electronic artists, festival and album reviews, and a companion CD of recordings tied to each issue. It appears three times a year. It is for musicians, composers and listeners who follow new and exploratory music.

NEUTRAL COLORS is a Japanese language magazine in which each issue takes a single theme, most recently health, and follows it through long reportage, interviews, travel pieces and photo stories from Japan and abroad. It is printed and bound in the publisher's own Yokohama workshop with a mix of offset and risograph, fold outs and inserts, so the object itself is part of the point. It suits readers of slow, essayistic magazines and people interested in independent print production.

New Escapologist is a small A5 essay magazine about getting out of things, from the office and consumer culture to debt and other obligations, in favour of a freer and more leisurely life. Each 88 page issue combines essays, columns, interviews and a readers' page of workplace complaints, with a colour cover and black and white interior. It is for readers of idler style anti work writing and practical minimalism.

NOTION is a London music and popular culture magazine built around cover interviews and fashion led shoots with musicians, actors, athletes and internet personalities, each print edition appearing with many different covers. Between numbered issues it publishes The Artists, print volumes profiling emerging acts. It is for readers who follow new music, youth culture and celebrity style.
